premises.text: Consumers currently lack leverage over the data collected about them by vendors
premises.evidence_span: we think that it's one-sided. Those with the vendors are the only ones that can be amassing and leveraging and tracking the data that's out there.

premises.text: Augmenting purchase data with personal stories can make shopping more meaningful for consumers
premises.evidence_span: we're augmenting the basic purchase data, the stuff that's like the what, the how much sort of thing, with the why, the real personal story behind what we're buying.

premises.text: Consumers can build a history of their purchases that includes personal insights
premises.evidence_span: I can start to slice it by when, where, what time, also by what I needed at the time, how I, how I, why I bought it at the time.

premises.text: Data analytics can provide meaningful insights by combining shopping history with other data
premises.evidence_span: show analytics around this data to make it meaningful for the customers, like taking the weather and mashing it up with your shopping history.

premises.text: Retailers can signal their interest in consumer data privacy through partnerships
premises.evidence_span: retail platforms, sort of a Powered by Schwob idea so that they tell... They're basically signaling to their customers that they're interested in not hoarding their data.

premises.text: Data portability allows consumers to leverage their data for better deals and personalized results
premises.evidence_span: the data actually is powerful when the customer can take all that they've amassed and leverage it back for something of value in return, better deals, loyalty points, VIP programs, and even better search results.

value.text: Consumers gain meaningful insights and leverage from their shopping data

notes: No traction metrics or external partnerships coded as premises.
